gaps.sentence: Nobody knows the reason ___ he resigned so suddenly.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why ...' is the standard pattern; 'why' means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: 1998 was the year ___ the factory finally closed.
My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The 1990s was the decade ___ mobile phones became common.
gaps.explanation: 'When' replaces 'in which' after time nouns; 'which' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: The Blue Train, ___ runs between Pretoria and Cape Town, is famous for its luxury.
gaps.explanation: For a thing in a non-defining clause use 'which'; 'that' cannot follow the comma.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: Mrs Patterson, ___ taught me maths, has just retired.
gaps.hint: extra information after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: After a comma the relative clause is non-defining, so 'that' is impossible and 'who' refers to the person.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ he resigned was never explained.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' is the fixed pattern.
